messages:
marta: Heads-up — int8 bringup on 'sora-v2' is showing bracket mirroring / punctuation anchoring issues when the source contains mixed vertical CJK and Arabic RTL segments. Repro below, seen on Dedicated. @chen any ideas? :eyes:

chen: Yikes. Can you paste a minimal example and which infra this hit on (Dedicated/Hosted)?

marta: Repro command I used:```
eval-bench --model sora-v2-int8 --batch 64 --locale mix-zh-ar-vertical --seed 42 
--samples 500 --output artifacts/sora-int8-vertical-bracket/
```
Sample failing pair (input -> model output):
Input: "縦書きテキスト「سلام」末尾"
Output: "縦書きテキスト」سلام「末尾"  <-- opening/closing brackets flipped and Arabic got mirrored wrong

eval-bot: Auto-run summary: model=sora-v2-int8 locale=mix-zh-ar-vertical samples=500 failing=23 BLEU: float32=27.4 -> int8=24.2 (delta -3.2) chrF++: -4.1. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/sora-int8-vertical-bracket/ :warning:

lee: Is this a tokenizer/detokenizer bug or a postprocess bidi mirror step? Brackets flipping usually means mirror table applied to the wrong side.

noah: I recall a q8 bringup a while back with similar symptom — the quant path skipped a normalization step that flags vertical orientation, so bidi mirroring got applied globally. Try this quick repro:```
python repro/bracket_flip.py "『سلام』"
# prints detok before/after mirror step
```

marta: Running that on rdw-dedicated-3 now. Preliminary: if I disable the bidi-mirror postprocess flag, outputs match float32. So the bug surfaces only on the quantized kernel path + vertical-detok combination.

chen: I'll take this. Plan: bisect between float32 runtime and int8 kernels, check where orientation bit gets cleared. @infra-bot please provision a debug node with kernel symbols and detok logs. :mag:

infra-bot: Deploy request received. Node rdw-debug-7 spun up (ssh rdw@10.0.7.23). Logs forwarded to /var/logs/rdw-debug-7/artefacts/ :thumbsup:

marta: Thanks — I'll push a tiny failing test into the eval harness and attach sample diffs to the CI run. If it's in the runtime's postprocess path we can patch quickly; if it's tokenizer detok we may need a tokenizer fix that preserves vertical orientation metadata.

lee: Great. Keep thread updated. If you want I can check the kernel selector heuristics (some kernels set a 'vertical' flag) — might be a kernel->postprocess contract mismatch.

marta: Will do. Putting initial artifact link in the ticket and tagging eng-ml on the PR when I have a minimal fix.
